summary: Provision shortlink namespace and scheduled retire-bot for ephemeral project channels
description:
Issue summary:
We need a centrally-managed shortlink namespace (rwd.link/<project>) for internal project runbooks and a scheduled Slack retire-bot that automatically marks ephemeral channels with a retirement tag and archives them after a configurable TTL.

Impact:
Currently each pod creates ad-hoc shortlinks (bit.ly, ad-hoc redirects) and relies on manual channel archiving. This leads to: stale links in runbooks, orphaned channels, audit/retention friction, and an operational burden on platform admins. The feature will reduce manual housekeeping and improve discoverability for runbooks and runbook-to-channel crosslinks.

Request:
1) Provision a new shortlink namespace under our Confluence domain (rwd.link) with per-project path templates and admin ACLs.
2) Create a Slack bot (retire-bot) scheduled job that: tags channels created by ephemeral templates, sends automated 7/3/1 day notices, reassigns channel ownership if original owner is inactive, and archives channels after TTL.
3) Add a small Jira admin console page to create mappings between Confluence spaces and shortlink paths and expose audit logs.

Background & context:
- Platform and Research pods have asked for predictable lifecycle policies to avoid leaking ephemeral channels into long-term directory.
- We already have a shortlink reverse-proxy in infra but no standardized namespace or admin UX.
- See Slack thread #pod-ops (link in related_confluence_pages) for requests and examples.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not include SSO or external sharing changes for Confluence pages. That is a follow-up if required.

Acceptance criteria:
- Shortlink namespace rwd.link is provisioned and reverse-proxied to Confluence/Custom redirects by project path.
- Admins can create a mapping from Confluence space key to rwd.link/<path> from a Jira admin page or a simple config file stored in the infra repo.
- Retire-bot is deployed to production with a configurable TTL (default 90 days), notice cadence (7/3/1 days), and an archive action that is reversible by admins for 14 days.
- Audit entries are emitted to the existing audit log stream and visible in the console.
- Documentation in Confluence created: shortlink-namespace runbook + retire-bot runbook.
acceptance_criteria: rwd.link namespace provisioned; admin mapping UI or config exists; retire-bot deployed with notice cadence and configurable TTL; audit logs emitted; docs created in Confluence; test scenario run showing archive and restore within 14 days.
steps_requested: 1) Infra: create DNS entry and reverse-proxy for rwd.link and route to Confluence shortlink handler. 2) Platform: add admin endpoint (Jira console page or repo config) to map Confluence space -> rwd.link path. 3) SRE: deploy retire-bot as a scheduled job in prod with settings: default TTL=90d, notices at 7/3/1 days, restore window=14d. 4) Docs: publish runbooks and add example runbook shortlinks. 5) QA: run end-to-end test (create ephemeral space and channel, validate notices, archive, restore).

investigation_notes: Checked existing shortlink reverse-proxy (infra service shortlink-proxy). It supports path-based routing and can be extended with a small mapping table. Slack bot framework exists (channel-manager) which supports scheduled tasks. No existing admin UI for mapping; simplest approach is a config file in infra repo + lightweight Jira admin page for convenience. Risk: need to ensure audit logs include channel archival actions to meet compliance requirements.

Retire-bot prototype running in staging; needs permission to post notices in templated channels and an admin endpoint for manual restore. Plan: complete infra changes, deploy retire-bot to prod with feature flag, run E2E, then flip feature flag. Post-deployment: add runbook and notify pods via #pod-ops.
